# komodo_variable (Resource)

Manages a Komodo global variable. Reference it as `[[NAME]]` in the environment, build args and other interpolated fields of stacks, deployments, builds and repos. Requires an admin API key.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# A plain variable, referenced as [[DOCKER_ROOT]] in stack/deployment config.
resource "komodo_variable" "docker_root" {
  name        = "DOCKER_ROOT"
  value       = "/opt/docker"
  description = "Base directory for stack data"
}

# A secret variable: hidden in Komodo's updates and logs.
resource "komodo_variable" "db_password" {
  name      = "POSTGRES_PASSWORD"
  value     = var.postgres_password
  is_secret = true
}

resource "komodo_stack" "app" {
  name      = "app"
  server_id = "Local"
  repo      = "myorg/app"

  environment = <<-EOT
    DATA_DIR=[[DOCKER_ROOT]]/app
    POSTGRES_PASSWORD=[[POSTGRES_PASSWORD]]
  EOT

  # Variables are resolved by name at deploy time, so make the dependency explicit.
  depends_on = [komodo_variable.docker_root, komodo_variable.db_password]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Variable name, as used in `[[NAME]]`. Komodo cannot rename a variable, so changing this replaces it.

### Optional

- `description` (String) Description shown in the Komodo UI.
- `is_secret` (Boolean) Mark the variable as a secret: Komodo hides its value in updates and logs, and from non-admin users.
- `value` (String, Sensitive) Variable value (up to 10000 characters). Always treated as sensitive by Terraform, whether or not is_secret is set. Komodo stores it unencrypted in its database.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Same as name. Variables have no separate ID in Komodo.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import an existing variable by its name.
terraform import komodo_variable.docker_root DOCKER_ROOT
```
